subscriptions.name: carraway
subscriptions.last_commit_message:
Say what is left today, this week, and in all — and stop crashing on exit

A budget's monthly figure does not answer the question actually being
asked, which is "can I buy this now". So a status carries three horizons:
what is left today, what is left before Sunday, and what is left of the
whole thing — plus what has already gone out today and this week.

"This week" is Monday to Sunday, not a rolling seven days, because that is
what the phrase means to everyone who is not a computer, and it is clipped
at both ends: never reaching back before the budget began, never running
past the day it closes. The weekly figure is this week's share rather than
the entire remaining balance, since spending the month's whole remainder
before Sunday is the thing it exists to prevent.

Both surfaces show it. The desktop leads with the three, with what has
gone, the sustainable rate, and the pace underneath. The phone gets the
same three as its headline, above the per-category lines.

And a crash, found by scripting the obvious thing: create a budget, quit
immediately. Creating one starts a publish, and Qt aborts if a QThread is
destroyed while still running — so the last thing Carraway did was
SIGABRT. Holding the threads kept them alive but nothing ever waited for
them. Now two hooks, because they catch different exits: aboutToQuit for a
running event loop, atexit for everything else.

subscriptions.last_commit_message:
The ES card folds — and a folded section still states its reading

Measured at 3,967px across fourteen sections, this card was 37% of the
page with two foldable blocks in it: the horizon bands had been applied to
the page and never to the single largest thing on it, so the reader got
navigation everywhere except where the scrolling actually is.

Seven sections are now CardSections, up from two. The card was unusually
well set up for this and nobody had noticed: it already computes a
one-sentence read for each major block — emRead, gammaRead, structureRead,
breadthRead, ladderRead — and rendered them as a Takeaway at the BOTTOM of
each block, so folding a section threw away the single line worth keeping.
CardSection gains collapsedSummary, and folded, that line is what remains.

That is what makes defaulting a section shut honest, and it is why the
rule changes. "Open by default, always" is right about a bare chevron and
wrong about a fold that still states its finding: it hides the evidence,
not the result. Two sections now default closed, and only two — the
base-rate tables and the session-path table are unconditional history over
thousands of sessions and cannot read differently at 15:00 than they did
at 09:30. Their summaries promote the parts that ARE about today: the
conditioned gap note, and path.live, which re-reads an unconditional 57%
gap fill as 20.7% at 11:45. Folding those blind would have hidden the only
live numbers in the block.

Two blocks removed. "Directional lean — swing horizon" rendered CTA flow
and the macro backdrop as their own mini-boards; both now have full rows
in BoardRoster one band down, under a heading that says they are
multi-day. "Macro headlines" was the second headline list on this page —
the driver card carries the other, from a different source, a screen away.
The one-sentence lean survives inside buildRead, where a clause of context
belongs. The old rule was "label the horizons"; it is now "put each block
in the horizon it belongs to", which is the axis the whole page runs on.

Verified in the browser: the two shut sections measure 62px each and cost
536px open (4,511 to 3,975), and the state round-trips. The card is now
55% of a shorter page — Reference levels at 986px and Expected move at
793px are the two largest blocks and both stay open because they develop
through the session.

rules(42-docusaurus): file 14 — the scaffold emits the one thing this pack bans

Rules currency pass file 14 to the full bar: D-062 spans, live multi-engine research,
author-blind second opinion (D-063), claims registered.

THE FINDING THAT MATTERS IS NOT IN THE PACK. `templates/docusaurus/Dockerfile.j2` ends
with `CMD ["npm","run","serve","--","--host","0.0.0.0","--port","3000"]` — a Node runtime

static hosting provider / CDN", and "the only responsibility of Docusaurus is to build
your site and emit static files in `build`". The template also ships NO nginx stage and
NO pagefind step — `grep -rn pagefind templates/docusaurus/ src/fabrik/scaffold.py`
returns nothing — so every scaffolded docs site starts with no search index at all and
the pack's whole § Search is unreachable. Scaffolding is the fleet beat, so this is FILED

PACK SIDE:
- The deferred D-064 class discharged: 4 unmarked `node:24` literals + every `bookworm`
  wrapped in marker spans. ⚠️ I checked the resulting tags EXIST before shipping them —
  `nginx:mainline-trixie` and `node:24-trixie-slim` both resolve on Docker Hub. Wrapping a
  codename in a span that yields an unpullable image would have been the worst possible

  `@getcanary/docusaurus-theme-search-pagefind` "exclusively" — 19 versions, newest
  published Oct 2024 (~23 months), peers `@docusaurus/core ^2||^3` and `react ^17||^18`.
  It is not deprecated and is in production use (Redux Toolkit ships it), and it still
  resolves against our template's pins today — but "exclusively" against an unmaintained
  peer range is a trap on the next major. Maintained alternative named, plus the floor
  fallback (pagefind CLI + swizzle SearchBar) marked as the one sanctioned swizzle so it

- The Algolia ban is now stated as OUR constraint rather than a verdict on Algolia: it is

Pagefind's own published figures are "tens of thousands of pages" and ~300kB total
payload on a 10,000-page site. Corrected in the pack AND in the claims row, with the
misattribution recorded there so the next reader knows the 25k figure was never the

The chain was created again on 2026-09-01. Every pinned value here still named
the previous one, so a reader who followed this repository built a node that

Board movement is now derived from git, not from my memory — check_plan.py --movement

He caught me claiming nine closes when the board had moved by one: four of the nine were the
PREVIOUS day's, and I had reported the day's achievement from recollection across a date boundary.
"make sense, keep better accounting going forward."

Made mechanical rather than intended, because that is the only thing that holds here.
`python scripts/check_plan.py --movement` compares the SET of task ids in PLAN.md at the last commit
BEFORE the operator's PT day began against the set now:

  === BOARD MOVEMENT — 2026-09-01 (PT), against a3f91d88 ===
    started 81 · now 82 · net +1
    CLOSED (4): #513, #562, #606, #609
    OPENED (5): #611, #612, #613, #615, #616

The subtlety that makes it correct: PLAN lines are edited constantly — appending a note removes and
re-adds the line — so a naive diff of +/- lines counts every edit as a close-and-reopen and inflates
both numbers. Comparing id sets is immune to that. The PT day boundary is used, never UTC, because
the harness clock is UTC and is not his day.

One honest blind spot printed in the output rather than hidden: a task opened AND closed the same
day appears in neither list, because it is in neither the start set nor the end set. #614 was one
today.

Three assertions pin it: set difference not line diff, the comparison point is the last commit
before the PT day, and the day boundary is the operator's timezone.

Suite 6795 green.

subscriptions.last_commit_message:
feat(folder): map Folder entity with lazy associations

Unidirectional: owner and parent are mapped, children are not. A folder
has one parent, but any number of children, and every real listing wants
sorting and paging -- which means a repository query rather than a
collection that loads everything the moment it is touched.

Both associations are explicitly LAZY. @ManyToOne defaults to EAGER,
which would load the whole ancestor chain on every folder read.

No JPA cascade. The database already removes subtrees in a single
statement via ON DELETE CASCADE; cascade = REMOVE would instead load
every descendant as an object and delete them one at a time.

Folders are built through named factories rather than constructors, so a
folder with neither owner nor parent cannot be expressed, and a child
takes its owner from its parent so the two cannot disagree.

Tests cover save and read-back, listing one level of children, finding a
user's root, and -- deliberately asserting a failure -- that touching a
lazy parent outside a transaction throws. That last one is what
open-in-view: false exists to surface.

Closes step 1.5.

新增注册停止按钮: 修复按钮永不显示 + 支持停止全部(含自动补号任务)

问题: 注册一旦开始无法停止。排查发现后端停止机制(stop_flags/procs/stop接口)早已存在, 前端也有停止按钮代码 —— 但按钮从来没显示过。

根因2(后端,残留): stop() 用 proc.terminate()/kill() 只杀主进程。Popen 用了 start_new_session=True, 子进程在独立进程组, 单独杀主进程会让 chromium 变孤儿残留, 继续占用 9222 调试端口 -> 下次注册启动浏览器直接失败。

根因3(能力缺失): 自动补号(auto_fill)自行调用 register(), task_id 只存在于后端内存, 前端拿不到, 单任务 stop 接口停不掉它。

- register.v3.js: 新增 regStopVisible() 统一控制顶部+日志面板两处按钮, 每次实时查询DOM(不缓存引用, 因面板会被 regLogShow 重建); 修正调用时机为 regLogShow 之后; 顶部『开始注册』旁新增常驻停止按钮; 去掉 confirm 弹窗(停止要快); 停止后继续轮询到终态而非立即断流; refresh.register 末尾查 /api/register/running 自动接管运行中任务(解决切tab后按钮消失)。

- registration_service.py: 新增 _kill_proc_group() 用 os.killpg 杀整组(与 _register_one 内做法一致) + proc.wait() 回收; stop() 改用之并兜底 pkill 清理9222残留; 新增 stop_all() 停全部running任务并清理 auto_fill 在途标记防止被立即拉起。

- main.py: 新增 POST /api/register/stop-all (可选 disable_auto_fill 关总开关) 与 GET /api/register/running (列出运行中任务供前端恢复状态)。

验证: 启停端到端实测 —— 启动count=1任务, 脚本跑到『3. 发码』时调 stop-all, 返回 stopped=[task_id], 任务状态转 stopped, 日志输出『🛑 子进程已终止(含浏览器进程组)』, 残留检查 chromium=0 / grok_auto_v7=0 / 9222未占用。

subscriptions.last_commit_message:
feat(packs): installing a country pack now leaves the workspace knowing its country

A project created while a country pack was active inherited the pack's
estimating methodology and nothing else. Everything else in the product that is
country-specific reads the project's country column: the markup region a bill
is seeded with, the CPM working calendar, the compliance-pack resolver and the
measurement system. All four answer "no opinion" when that column is unset, so
installing the Hungarian pack fitted out the cascade and left every one of them
saying nothing was known about the market, on a workspace that had just been
told which market it was for. From this release, a project created under a
country pack takes the pack's country when the person creating it named none.

Only when they named none. An explicit choice always wins, and the fill is
recorded in metadata as country_from_pack, because a country the product filled
in is not the same fact as a country the user typed and the nullable column
exists precisely so those stop being one row.

The market comes from a new market_country_code on the manifest rather than
from a reading of metadata['country'] at the call site, so there is one
definition of what counts as a market. It returns nothing for a pack that names
no country, for a malformed code, and for 'XX', which reads like a country code
and means the opposite of one. That marker had been a bare literal in two
places and now has a name, since a hand-rolled copy of this reading is exactly
the thing that would miss it.

Three country packs shipped no methodology at all: Canada, New Zealand and
South Africa. Each has had a template in the catalogue the whole time and
nothing was naming it, so a project created under those packs opened on the
flat international default while the pack itself declared the country's
currency, its cost regions and its standards. All three templates are still the
neutral international method carrying the local currency and consumption-tax
rate rather than a national convention, and they say so of themselves; the
manifests say so too. Naming them is strictly better than a method that carries
no country, and each turns national with no edit here the moment the markup
table states that country's stack.

The gate that caught the first two of these (Brazil and Saudi) could not have
caught these three: it fires only where a national markup stack exists, and
none of the three has one. Rather than write a second gate beside it, it grew a
second tier. The strict tier is unchanged, and the new one asks only that a
pack selling a country names that country's template, national or neutral.
Between them the tiers now cover 16 of the 20 packs; the four they do not touch
name no market at all, which is the sector packs and the industry pack. The
floor is on the sum of the two populations rather than on either, because packs
move from the neutral tier to the strict one as the markup table grows and a
tier that legitimately empties must not read as a broken gate.

Both new checks are red on real wrong states rather than on hypotheses. The
second tier was run against the three manifests as they stood at HEAD and
rejected all three, plus a pack pointing at another market's template. The
inheritance guard was run against four ways of writing it: unguarded, guarded
on the pack only, guarded the wrong way round so that it fills in only when a
country was already chosen, and correct. It judged all four right, and it
rejects a call site that goes back to reading the metadata key itself.

subscriptions.last_commit_message: Add max-width: 100% to card-field-image so it can't overlap cards Reported directly: "the data cards in some cards are able to overlap, specifically with an image larger than the column. This should not be possible, is this a flex or a grid? Maybe our image should have max-width: 100% by default?" gateway/data-cards-body's own grid is a real CSS Grid (supports.layout.default.type: "grid", not flex), and the diagnosis was exactly right: neither wp_get_attachment_image() (the 'array'/'id' Return Format branch) nor this block's own hand-built tag ('url' format) had any width constraint beyond the registered size's own fixed width/height HTML attributes -- and a CSS Grid item's own implicit min-width: auto means an oversized child can force it wider than its own track, the classic "min-size auto" overflow gotcha. This block never had a stylesheet of its own at all before now. Added one: .gateway-card-field-image img { max-width: 100%; height: auto; } (a descendant selector, reaching the whether or not it's wrapped in this block's own optional Link Settings ). height: auto alongside max-width: 100% is the standard responsive-image pairing, keeping aspect ratio correct as width shrinks rather than distorting against the fixed height attribute. A configured Aspect Ratio already sets width:100%;height:100%; directly as an inline style on the , which always wins the cascade regardless of load order, so this new default never fights that feature. Since this block had no view.js either (nothing interactive on the front end), added one that exists solely to get style.scss compiled into both contexts -- the same shape gateway/data-cards-header's own identical-purpose view.js already has -- and added "style" to block.json. Verified with a successful production build (confirmed build/style-view.css contains the compiled rule) and the full existing PHP regression suite (unaffected -- only a render.php docblock touched, no logic). README updated. The actual "an oversized image now shrinks to fit instead of overlapping the next card" behavior needs manual verification in a real block editor + browser. Pin the refusal that decides who may speak for a marketplace

The signature beside a marketplace says who publishes it, and the one
thing that must not be possible is a second signer taking that over by
running the same command. `marketplace sign` already refuses — and
nothing tested it, which is how a load-bearing refusal quietly becomes
optional the next time somebody edits that branch.

Both halves are pinned: the command exits usage rather than signing,
and the file it declined to replace is byte-for-byte unchanged. The
sequence is checked too, because a refusal that still bumped it would
leave every machine that had seen the old catalog rejecting the next
real publish as a rollback.

Test only. What this replaces was a --rotate-key flag I had started for
the lost-key case: new format field, new flag, a second signature on
the envelope. That is a key-ceremony feature invented ahead of the
decision it depends on, and the recovery it automates is one command
run once. Dropped rather than finished.

Filter the names that are not names, and the camps that are not yours

Found by looking at what the new tier actually pinned, before anyone else
saw it. Dropping the operator requirement let through five Alberta campsites
called "Please Pack Out Your Garbage" — mappers using the name field for the
sign standing there, which is a fair thing to do to a map and a terrible
thing to put on a pin. The operator gate had been hiding them by accident,
and removing it took the cover off.

Three filters, all in the strict direction, because the cost of being wrong
here is a real campground staying off the map and the cost of being wrong the
other way is somebody pulling into a children's camp at dusk:

  - Signage. A name that opens with an instruction, or says pack out, leave
    no trace, closed.
  - Somebody's programme rather than somewhere a passing camper can sleep:
    a children's ranch, a scout camp, a church or bible camp, a YMCA. All
    genuinely tourism=camp_site, all genuinely free, none of them free TO
    YOU. Tim Horton Children's Ranch was pinned as a free campground.
  - access=private/no/customers/members, which says the same thing in a tag.

And one sub-unit pattern: "Camping Area 1" through "Camping Area 7" arrived
as seven pins stacked on one Alberta campground. The existing rule wanted the
number to follow "camp" or "site" directly and these have a word in between.

The thirteen rows that had already stored are deleted. Worth writing down:
THE INGEST NEVER REMOVES A ROW THAT STOPS QUALIFYING — it upserts and moves
on — so a filter tightened after a run leaves its mistakes on the map until
somebody deletes them by hand, as here.
